messages:
Marta: quick follow-up from the RFC thread — I'm prototyping a 'soft-degrade' mode for active/active when cross-region write routing fails due to capacity or legal flags. sketch: prefer local writes for low-risk tenants, escrow high-risk writes (ack locally but mark for cross-region reconciliation), emit consent headers. want quick sanity check and operator rollback plan.

Liam: sounds reasonable. main question: how do we decide "high-risk" vs "low-risk" at runtime? header? tenant tag?

Marta: tenant tag + tenant-level policy in the control plane. we already have a consent matrix service so we can fetch tenant.consent_level on request.

Sara: two immediate concerns: (1) correctness of tenant-level reconciliation (ordering, idempotency), (2) SLA expectations — acks for escrowed writes might imply perceived success for the caller. need explicit response codes.

Raj: +1. for (1) i'd suggest using an "escrow" queue with monotonic write_id per-tenant and idempotent ops. store per-tenant tombstone map to detect duplicates.

Marta: agreed. implementation sketch: local path for writes:
```
if tenant.residency == "strict":
  return 409 (write-deferred)
else if tenant.residency == "prefers-local":
  accept locally, enqueue->escrow if cross-region forward fails
else:
  normal cross-region forward
```
we probably want a 2xx for local-accepted but with a flag in the response body when "escrowed" so clients know.

Liam: don't want to break existing clients. so prefer returning 202 with header X-Write-Status: escrowed or X-Residency-Mode.

Olivia: legal check — anything that persists PII in escrow across borders requires consent. can we encrypt escrowed payloads with tenant-specific KMS keys and restrict where keys can be used?

Raj: yes, KMS-per-tenant + HSM-backed keys in region of residency. escrow proxies should store ciphertext only and decryption only happens in resident region during reconciliation.

Sara: telemetry: need counters for escrow enqueue rate, average escrow-to-reconcile latency, and how often reconciliation fails. add alert if escrow backlog > 10k or oldest > 1hr.

OpsBot: deploy canary: residency-soft-degrade v0.1 -> canary on edge-03 at 4072001300. monitor: escrow-queue-depth, forward-fail-rate, reconciliation-errors.

Marta: rollout plan idea:
- canary in eu region with 2 tenants flagged as "prefers-local"
- run for 2 hours, validate no data exfiltration and reconciliation latency < 5m
- widen to multi-region small percentage
- if backlog grows or reconciliation error rate > 1% -> automatic rollback

Liam: rollback implementation: feature-flag toggle (control-plane) that forces 'reject local-accept' fallback (return 409 to clients). that way we stop accepting escrowed writes immediately.

Olivia: add a legal-safe mode toggle which also disables storing escrow payloads outside resident-region even encrypted. i.e. forbids cross-region escrow writes entirely.

Raj: minor infra note: escrow queues are append-only S3 buckets + an indexer that streams to reconciliation workers. ensure lifecycle TTL > 7d for debugging. also pre-warm reconciliation workers to avoid burst backlog.

Sara: action items: (1) Marta: PR for control-plane tenant policy + response header changes; (2) Raj: prototype escrow queue + idempotency tokens; (3) Liam: client-compatibility doc + suggested response codes; (4) Olivia: legal checklist & KMS integration plan.

Marta: thanks all — i'll open issues and a short explainer. emoji :thumbsup:

Liam: small test idea: simulate region-partition in chaos rig and verify canary tenants see 202+escrow, others get 409.

OpsBot: canary results summary at 4072001500: escrow enqueue rate 12/min, avg reconcile latency 2m30s, no repro legal-flag violations, no reconciliation failures.

Olivia: good preliminary signal. please keep KMS logs for audit.

Marta: closing loop: I'll schedule follow-up sync Tues to decide production rollout thresholds. thanks! :sparkles:
